findings.title: ConsoleEx is a parallel renderer universe — does not implement ITuiRenderer
findings.description: ConsoleEx (src/Harbor.Tui.ConsoleEx, ~11.5k LOC) is built as a standalone frame-loop renderer with its own widgets, streaming, input pipeline, and REPL runner (apps/Harbor.App.Cli/Repl/ConsoleExReplRunner.cs, 435 LOC). It completely bypasses the ITuiRenderer / BaseTuiRenderer abstraction. Changes to BaseTuiRenderer (new views, event handling, placement logic) do not propagate to ConsoleEx.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an adapter layer (ConsoleExTuiRenderer) that wraps the existing ConsoleEx frame loop and implements ITuiRenderer / IInteractiveTuiRenderer, or extract a shared IRenderLoop abstraction that both BaseTuiRenderer and ConsoleEx can implement.

findings.title: AnsiTuiRenderer and PlainTuiRenderer are ~90% identical
findings.description: Both renderers extend BaseTuiRenderer and override ShouldRenderPlacement, RenderAsync, ReadLineAsync, WriteAsync, WriteLineAsync, ClearAsync with nearly identical logic. The only meaningful difference is the ITuiRenderContext implementation (ANSI escape codes vs plain text). The private static RenderLiveToken methods are copy-pasted.
findings.recommendation: Extract a common StreamingTuiRenderer base class that holds the shared event-switch and RenderLiveToken logic, parameterized by ITuiRenderContext factory. AnsiRenderContext and PlainRenderContext become pure context implementations.

findings.title: Avalonia and Blazor do not use ITuiRenderer — separate Ui.Framework architecture
findings.description: Avalonia (apps/Harbor.App.Avalonia) and Blazor (contrib/apps/Harbor.App.Blazor) both use Harbor.Ui.Framework (UiStore, DefaultUiProjector, ChatStreamingPresenter, reducers) instead of ITuiRenderer. They subscribe to agent events through a completely different pipeline (TEA/MVU pattern vs event-bus-driven view dispatch). This means any change to agent event semantics, view placement logic, or builtin views in BaseTuiRenderer has no effect on desktop/web platforms.
findings.recommendation: Define a cross-platform IRenderTarget or IPlatformRenderer interface that both BaseTuiRenderer (for TUI) and UiRenderEngine / Blazor components (for desktop/web) implement. Route AgentEvents through a shared dispatcher that delegates to the platform-specific target.

findings.title: Blazor has no renderer-specific unit tests
findings.description: Blazor test project (contrib/tests/Harbor.App.Blazor.Tests) contains only a single 178-line DI test (ProgramDiTests.cs). There are no unit tests for ChatViewModel, UiStore integration, ThemeService, or any rendering behavior. The E2E test (contrib/tests/Harbor.E2E.App.Blazor/BlazorE2ETests.cs, 149 lines) is minimal.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for ChatViewModel.SendAsync, UiStore state transitions, ThemeService, and Razor component rendering. Add screenshot-diff or component snapshot tests for MarkdownRenderer, ChatBubble, StatusBar, and TokenUsageChart.

findings.title: Avalonia UiRenderEngine lacks dedicated unit tests
findings.description: UiRenderEngine (apps/Harbor.App.Avalonia/Services/UiRenderEngine.cs, 268 LOC) contains complex reconciliation logic for ReconcileTimeline, ReconcileToolCalls, and ReconcileLines, but has no dedicated unit tests. Avalonia.Tests covers VMs and components, but not the render-engine projection layer.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for UiRenderEngine.ReconcileTimeline, ReconcileToolCalls, ReconcileLines, and DeriveStatus using a fake DefaultUiProjector and UiState snapshots.

findings.title: NotificationTuiRenderer is a placeholder — no terminal rendering
findings.description: NotificationTuiRenderer (src/Harbor.Tui.Notifications/NotificationTuiRenderer.cs, 287 LOC) implements BaseTuiRenderer but all rendering methods are no-ops. ShouldRenderPlacement returns false. It only fires OS notifications via notify-send / osascript / msg.exe. While this is by design for background agents, the builtin views (StatusBarView, ChatHistoryView, InputView, DiffPreviewView) are still registered and bound to VMs but never rendered, wasting initialization cycles.
findings.recommendation: Either skip builtin view registration when the renderer is non-visual, or document explicitly that NotificationTuiRenderer is a 'listener-only' renderer that should not inherit BaseTuiRenderer's view-dispatch behavior.

findings.title: No screenshot-diff / visual regression tests for any platform
findings.description: ConsoleEx has golden-file tests (ScreenshotHashTests.cs, GoldenChatScreenTests.cs) but no screenshot-diff regression. Avalonia and Blazor have zero visual regression tests. There is no shared screenshot-diff harness that could catch rendering regressions across platforms.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a cross-platform screenshot-diff test harness. For TUI, extend TerminalScreenshotRenderer. For Avalonia, use the existing headless driver. For Blazor, add Playwright-based screenshot capture with pixel-diff against golden baselines.

findings.title: Markdown rendering is duplicated across ConsoleEx, Avalonia, and Blazor
findings.description: Each platform implements its own markdown renderer: ConsoleEx has StreamingMarkdownRenderer + MarkdownBlockParser (src/Harbor.Tui.ConsoleEx/Widgets/Markdown/), Avalonia has MarkdownBlockRenderer + MarkdownInlineRenderer (apps/Harbor.App.Avalonia/Views/Controls/Markdown/), and Blazor has MarkdownRenderer.razor. There is no shared markdown abstraction.
findings.recommendation: Extract a Harbor.Markdown.Abstractions layer with a shared IMarkdownParser / IMarkdownRenderer contract. Each platform provides only a view-layer adapter that consumes parsed markdown ASTs.

findings.title: Blazor is a demo shell without real agent integration
findings.description: Blazor ChatViewModel (contrib/apps/Harbor.App.Blazor/ViewModels/ViewModels.cs) falls back to a local demo transcript when no agent is wired up. SendAsync just echoes an 'unconfigured' message after 150ms. There is no real event bus subscription, no UiStore-driven chat streaming, and no integration with Harbor.Application.
findings.recommendation: Wire Blazor ChatViewModel to the real UiStore / event bus so it renders live agent streams instead of the hardcoded demo transcript. Alternatively, mark the project as a 'shell demo' to set expectations.

findings.title: No unit tests for NotificationTuiRenderer or its backends
findings.description: NotificationTuiRenderer and the platform-specific backends (LinuxNotifySendBackend, MacOsascriptBackend, WindowsToastBackend) have zero unit tests. The backend detection logic (DetectBackend) is also untested.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests for backend detection, notification firing, and error handling. Use process-start mocking or a test-specific INotificationBackend factory.

findings.title: Event propagation differs across all platforms with no shared contract
findings.description: TUI renderers receive events via event-bus subscription in ReplRunner (eventBus.Subscribe(renderer.RenderAsync)). Avalonia uses UiStore + reducers. Blazor uses UiStore + Razor binding. ConsoleEx uses its own ConsoleExReplRunner frame loop. There is no IEventRouter or IPlatformEventSink interface that unifies how AgentEvents reach the renderer.
findings.recommendation: Introduce IPlatformEventSink (or similar) with a single Dispatch(AgentEvent) method. Each platform implements it: TuiEventSink calls renderer.RenderAsync, AvaloniaEventSink dispatches to UiStore, BlazorEventSink invokes BlazorDispatcherAdapter. ReplRunner and ConsoleExReplRunner both resolve IPlatformEventSink instead of reaching directly for renderers.

findings.title: RazorConsole, SpectreTui, TerminalGui, and Sixel renderers exist only in contrib/
findings.description: Additional renderers (contrib/tui/Harbor.Tui.RazorConsole, Harbor.Tui.SpectreTui, Harbor.Tui.TerminalGui, Harbor.Tui.Sixel) are in the contrib tree, not in src/. They have test projects in contrib/tests/Harbor.Tui.Contrib.Tests/. This is not necessarily a bug, but it means they are not part of the primary build or CI pipeline for the main solution.
findings.recommendation: Document the intended lifecycle for contrib renderers. If they are meant to be first-class, migrate them into src/ and include them in Harbor.slnx. If they are experimental, gate them behind a feature flag and add CI checks.

renderer_inventory.name: ConsoleEx
renderer_inventory.notes: Standalone frame-loop architecture. Bypasses BaseTuiRenderer entirely. Rich widget set (markdown, diff, timeline, spinners). Extensive test coverage but no shared renderer contract.

renderer_inventory.name: AnsiTuiRenderer
renderer_inventory.notes: Full ANSI color/style support. Extends BaseTuiRenderer. Good test coverage. High code duplication with PlainTuiRenderer.

renderer_inventory.name: PlainTuiRenderer
renderer_inventory.notes: No ANSI codes, designed for piping/CI. Near-duplicate of AnsiTuiRenderer with plain-text context.

renderer_inventory.name: NotificationTuiRenderer
renderer_inventory.notes: Non-interactive; fires OS notifications only. All render methods are no-ops. Views are registered but never rendered.

renderer_inventory.name: Avalonia (UiRenderEngine)

test_coverage.unit_tests: partial (VM/component tests exist, no render-engine tests)

renderer_inventory.notes: Uses Harbor.Ui.Framework (UiStore + DefaultUiProjector). Full desktop app with 30+ views/viewmodels. No shared renderer abstraction with TUI.

renderer_inventory.name: Blazor (Razor Components)
renderer_inventory.notes: Demo shell with local transcript fallback. Uses Harbor.Ui.Framework but without real agent streaming integration. Minimal test coverage.

missing_renderers.name: ConsoleExTuiRenderer (adapter)
missing_renderers.reason: ConsoleEx should implement ITuiRenderer / IInteractiveTuiRenderer to participate in the standard renderer lifecycle and share view-dispatch logic with Ansi/Plain/Notifications.

missing_renderers.name: Cross-platform screenshot-diff harness
missing_renderers.reason: No visual regression testing infrastructure exists for any platform.

missing_renderers.name: Shared markdown rendering abstraction
missing_renderers.reason: Markdown rendering logic is independently reimplemented in ConsoleEx, Avalonia, and Blazor.
